workflow_metadata.name: Reflow Meta-Analysis Workflow (Self-Sharpening Knife)
workflow_metadata.description: Run Reflow's own workflows (01d-functional_analysis.json) ON Reflow itself to detect gaps, context bottlenecks, and architectural issues, then use gap closure tools to propose and apply fixes - creating a truly self-improving system
workflow_metadata.purpose: Formalize the repeatable process of having Reflow analyze itself using functional architecture methodology with context consumption tracking, then apply implementation fixes to continuously improve
workflow_metadata.key_innovation: v3.0.0: Truly self-referential - Reflow runs its own workflows (01d-functional_analysis.json) ON ITSELF, uses system_of_systems_graph_v2.py for graph analysis, and applies gap closure tools (reflow_gap_closure.py) to propose and implement fixes - making Reflow a fully self-improving 'self-sharpening knife'
workflow_metadata.when_to_use: Run this workflow after any significant updates to Reflow workflows, tools, or templates to ensure no new issues introduced AND to continuously improve existing implementation

required_conditions: Reflow repository exists and is accessible
All Reflow workflows, tools, and templates present
not_required: Foundational documents (Reflow itself is the system being analyzed)
System root separate from reflow root (same directory)

standard.description: Standard meta-analysis - full functional architecture analysis with context tracking

quick.description: Quick check - run only functional architecture analysis on existing functional_architecture.json

workflow_steps.description: Configure working_memory.json for meta-analysis where Reflow analyzes itself

framework_configuration.framework_name: Functional Flow Framework (based on Decision Flow)

context_aware_analysis.rationale: AI agents have limited context windows - must track consumption

actions.note: This tells Reflow it's analyzing itself using the Functional Flow Framework

workflow_steps.name: Define Functional Requirements (SE-00A)
workflow_steps.description: Document WHAT Reflow must do (functional requirements) by analyzing mission statement, user scenarios, and workflows

actions.purpose: Understand what Reflow is supposed to do

actions.method: Analyze each user scenario and workflow to identify required capabilities
outputs: List of functional requirements (FR-001, FR-002, etc.)
Traceability matrix: User Scenarios → Functional Requirements

actions.template: Use template structure shown in example specs/functional/functional_requirements.json

gates.name: Functional Requirements Completeness
checks: All user scenarios covered by requirements

workflow_steps.name: Define Functional Architecture with Context Tracking (SE-00B)
workflow_steps.description: Document HOW Reflow achieves functional requirements through process flows with AI agent context consumption tracking

actions.description: Identify major functional flows in Reflow
examples: Workflow Execution Flow
Context Management Flow
Architecture Generation Flow
Graph Analysis Flow
Validation Flow
Functional Architecture Flow (new in v2.1.0)
Documentation Generation Flow
Context Bottleneck Analysis Flow
actions.note: Each flow represents a major capability

actions.description: Decompose each flow into atomic functions
actions.method: Break down flows into discrete functions (read, process, generate, validate, decide, iterate)

actions.note: Context consumption as edge weight enables bottleneck analysis

actions.description: Estimate context consumption for each function
actions.note: Estimates based on typical file sizes and output lengths

actions.template: Use template structure shown in example specs/functional/functional_architecture.json
required_sections: functions (array of function objects with context_consumption)

actions.description: SELF-REFERENTIAL: Invoke 01d-functional_analysis.json workflow on Reflow itself (RECOMMENDED)
actions.purpose: Use Reflow's own functional analysis workflow to analyze Reflow - truly self-referential meta-analysis
actions.note: This executes FA-01 through FA-07 on Reflow itself, using Reflow to analyze Reflow
actions.alternative: Manual execution (META-03-A01 through META-03-A05) if workflow invocation not desired
benefits: Truly self-referential - Reflow analyzes itself using its own methodology
Ensures consistency between Reflow's workflows and its own architecture
Automatic stakeholder validation (FA-04), technical analysis (FA-05), and iterative refinement (FA-06)

gates.name: Functional Architecture Completeness
checks: All functional requirements implemented by functions
All functions have context consumption estimates
Major flows documented with entry/exit points

workflow_steps.name: Analyze Functional Architecture for Context Bottlenecks
workflow_steps.description: Run automated analysis to detect gaps, context bottlenecks, circular dependencies, and inefficiencies

analyses_performed: Context path analysis (cumulative context along all paths)

actions.console_output: Analysis prints to console with summary statistics

severity_levels.CRITICAL: Context bottlenecks (>160k tokens), missing required functions, unreachable critical flows
severity_levels.WARNING: Context approaching limits (>140k), dead-end functions, high complexity

actions.purpose: Generate NetworkX graph and perform comprehensive graph-theoretic analysis
analyses_performed: Knowledge gap detection (6 types: orphaned interfaces, missing nodes, dark matter, structural holes, circular deps, isolated components)
Context flow analysis (cumulative context along paths)
Cycle detection (feedback loops vs circular dependencies)
DAG validation (functional architecture should be acyclic)
actions.note: This complements analyze_functional_architecture.py by providing graph-theoretic insights
expected_outputs: Console output with NetworkX analysis results

outputs: Console output with summary and recommendations

workflow_steps.name: Address Critical Issues (Iterative Refinement)
workflow_steps.description: Fix critical issues found in analysis before proceeding

actions.description: Refine functional architecture to address issues

context_bottlenecks: Break long paths into separate sessions with context refresh points
Implement lazy loading for high-context functions (e.g., F-030 Load All Architecture Files)
Summarize outputs instead of returning full details
Stream large file reads instead of loading entirely
unreachable_functions: Add missing dependencies to make functions reachable
Document separate execution contexts (some functions may be standalone)
orphaned_functions: Add connections to integrate into flows
unintentional_cycles: Redesign flow to break circular dependency
Add termination conditions to iterative loops

actions.loop_condition: If critical issues remain, return to META-05-A02

actions.description: Automated gap closure proposals using matrix analysis and architecture linking (NEW v3.13.0)
actions.purpose: Automatically propose solutions for functional gaps using mathematical reasoning (B = C × A⁻¹) and architecture linking
gap_types_addressed: Dead-end functions - propose output handlers or downstream functions
Incomplete flows - use matrix analysis to find missing intermediate functions

proposed_solution.rationale: Matrix analysis indicates F-010 and F-015 should connect to F-042

actions.note: Proposals are NOT auto-applied - LLM/human must review before accepting
actions.integration: Proposals can be applied in META-05-A02 or deferred to META-05B for implementation-level fixes
benefits: Mathematical reasoning (matrix analysis) identifies missing intermediate functions
Architecture linking discovers missing connections based on patterns
Reduces manual effort in identifying gap solutions

gates.name: Critical Issues Resolved
gates.note: Warnings are acceptable, but CRITICAL issues must be resolved

workflow_steps.name: Implementation Refinement (Fix Workflows, Tools, Schemas)
workflow_steps.description: Apply architectural insights by fixing actual implementation files (workflows, tools, schemas) based on analysis results to create a 'self-sharpening knife' that continuously improves itself
workflow_steps.rationale: Functional architecture analysis identifies issues in the spec. This step fixes the actual implementation to resolve root causes, closing the improvement loop.
workflow_steps.critical_insight: Without this step, meta-analysis only updates the architectural description (functional_architecture.json) but doesn't fix the actual implementation (workflows/*.json, tools/*.py, schemas/*.json). This step makes Reflow self-improving.

actions.description: Map functional architecture issues to implementation files
actions.purpose: Identify which files need to be edited to fix root causes

context_bottlenecks_in_workflow_executio: workflows/*.json - Add context refresh points between phases
workflows/*.json - Break long workflows into sub-workflows
tools/*.py - Implement lazy loading instead of loading all files at once
missing_error_handling: workflows/*.json - Add error handlers to quality gates
tools/*.py - Add try/except blocks with proper error flows
workflows/*.json - Add error_handling actions to workflow steps
orphaned_functions: workflows/*.json - Add missing workflow steps that implement orphaned functions
Document as standalone if intentionally separate
high_context_functions: tools/*.py - Refactor F-030 (Load All Architecture Files) to load on-demand
tools/*.py - Summarize outputs instead of returning full details
tools/*.py - Stream large files instead of loading entirely
workflows/*.json - Split high-context steps into smaller steps
unreachable_functions: workflows/*.json - Add missing workflow steps to create execution path
Use gap closure proposals from META-05-A04 (reflow_gap_closure.py) for connector function recommendations
Remove from functional_architecture.json if truly unused
dead_end_functions: workflows/*.json - Add downstream workflow steps that consume dead-end function outputs
Use gap closure proposals from META-05-A04 for output handler recommendations
Remove if outputs are intentionally terminal (e.g., final report generation)
incomplete_flows: workflows/*.json - Add missing intermediate workflow steps
Use matrix analysis from META-05-A04 to identify missing intermediate functions (B = C × A⁻¹)
tools/*.py - Implement missing functions identified by gap closure analysis
unintentional_cycles: workflows/*.json - Redesign workflow routing to break circular dependency
tools/*.py - Add termination conditions to iterative loops

actions.output: List of files to edit with specific changes needed

actions.for_each_issue: Edit workflow definitions to address architectural issues
examples: Add context refresh point: Insert step with action 'context_refresh' between META-03 and META-07
Break meta-analysis workflow: Split into 99a-meta_analysis_part1.json and 99b-meta_analysis_part2.json if paths exceed 160k
Add missing error handlers: Add 'error_handling' object to quality gates
Reduce step context: Split large actions into multiple smaller actions
actions.validation: Validate workflow JSON schema after edits

actions.for_each_issue: Refactor tools to reduce context consumption or improve efficiency
examples: Lazy loading: Refactor analyze_functional_architecture.py to load architecture files on-demand instead of all at once
Streaming: Refactor system_of_systems_graph_v2.py to stream large files instead of loading into memory
Summarization: Refactor tools to return summaries (e.g., 'Found 10 issues' instead of listing all 10)
Error handling: Add try/except blocks with proper error flows to all analysis tools
Modularization: Break large functions (>50 lines) into smaller helper functions

actions.for_each_issue: Update data schemas and templates based on architectural changes
examples: Add 'context_refresh' field to workflow step schema if adding context refresh points
Update architecture template to include error_handling sections
Add new fields required by updated workflows or tools

actions.purpose: Verify that implementation fixes work correctly and don't introduce regressions
tests: Dry-run updated workflows on test data to verify executability
Run tools with updated parameters to verify outputs match expected format
Integration test: Run full workflow end-to-end to verify all pieces work together
Regression test: Verify existing functionality still works (e.g., SE workflow still completes)

actions.description: Update functional_architecture.json to reflect implementation changes
actions.rationale: Implementation fixes may change functions, context estimates, dependencies, or flows
updates_needed: Update context_consumption estimates based on actual refactored code
Add/remove functions if workflow steps were added/removed
Update function_dependencies if execution flow changed
Update functional_flows if new flows created or flows split
actions.purpose: Keep functional architecture synchronized with actual implementation
Verify that implementation fixes resolved the architectural issues
expected_results: Overall max_context_path reduced compared to previous iteration
actions.loop_condition: If critical issues remain in implementation, return to META-05B-A01
actions.termination: Analysis shows no critical issues, implementation validated

outputs: Updated schemas/*.json and templates/*.json files (if needed)
Test results confirming implementation fixes work

gates.name: Implementation Validated (Self-Sharpening Complete)
checks: All workflows/*.json files valid and executable
All tools/*.py files pass syntax check (python3 -m py_compile)
Integration tests pass (workflows can execute tools successfully)
Functional architecture analysis shows critical issues resolved
No regressions introduced (existing functionality still works)
Context consumption reduced for high-context paths
gates.success_message: Reflow has successfully sharpened itself - implementation fixes applied and validated

workflow_steps.self_sharpening_note: This step is the 'sharpening' mechanism that makes Reflow self-improving. It closes the loop: analyze → detect → FIX IMPLEMENTATION → re-analyze → validate.

trigger_events: After adding new tools that consume context
Quarterly as part of technical health check

critical_reminders: This is Reflow analyzing ITSELF - system_root = reflow_root
v3.0.0: INVOKE 01d-functional_analysis.json ON REFLOW - truly self-referential (META-03-A06)
v3.0.0: RUN system_of_systems_graph_v2.py for graph-theoretic analysis (META-04-A04)
v3.0.0: USE reflow_gap_closure.py to propose gap solutions with mathematical reasoning (META-05-A04)
Context consumption is the PRIMARY metric - track it for all functions
Context bottlenecks (>160k tokens) are CRITICAL issues that block AI agents
Not all unreachable functions are problems - some operate in separate contexts
Cycles may be intentional (iterative refinement loops) or problematic (circular dependencies) - review each
Focus on functional CAPABILITIES, not implementation details
Gap closure proposals are NOT auto-applied - review before accepting
common_mistakes: Treating Reflow as a normal system instead of meta-analysis
NOT invoking 01d-functional_analysis.json on Reflow (manual decomposition instead of using Reflow's own workflows)
NOT using gap closure tools (missing automated gap solution proposals)
Not tracking context consumption for functions
Missing high-context functions (file reads, large generations)
Not iterating when critical issues found
Creating visualizations without reviewing analysis first
Auto-applying gap closure proposals without review
llm_agent_guidance.workflow_philosophy: v3.0.0: Meta-analysis is TRULY self-referential - Reflow uses its OWN workflows (01d-functional_analysis.json) and tools (system_of_systems_graph_v2.py, reflow_gap_closure.py) to analyze and improve itself. This validates that Reflow's methodology works correctly and creates a self-improving system. Context consumption is the critical constraint that must be monitored.
self_referential_benefits: Ensures Reflow follows its own best practices
Automatic gap detection and closure proposals using mathematical reasoning
Graph-theoretic insights from NetworkX analysis (centrality, community, cycles, connectivity)
Truly self-improving - Reflow sharpens itself using its own tools
